A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DSO and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E. Full text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original DSO experiments on VLMs and LLMs, including benchmark comparisons, sparsity analysis and prompt robustness.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–5 and the experimental analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The fairness reward, sparse linear activation interventions, optimization procedure and inference-time steering remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions use SocialCounterfactuals and GenderBias-VL for occupation identification and hiring, SynthBias for coreference resolution, and MMMU/MMLU for capability evaluation. Prompt-variation coverage also remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–5 retain the same base-model, prompting, CAA and ITI comparisons against DSO. No comparator is added, removed or revised.

E3.justification: The model configurations, ambiguous/unambiguous data construction, 600-sample training budget, metrics, prompts and steering-strength selection remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices B–D.

E4.justification: The sparsity analysis in Figure 5, prompt robustness analysis in Figure 7 and KL-divergence analyses in Figures 8–9 are unchanged. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: SEM reporting, figure error bars and run/seed disclosures remain unchanged. The recoloring of one Table 2 cell changes its displayed classification, not the uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 reclassifies Qwen2.5-7B DSO at lambda=0.4: its unambiguous don't-know rate, still 10.3% (0.2), changes from red ('metric worsened') to yellow ('within SEM of base model'). This changes one qualitative comparison; numerical results and plotted trends remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, assumptions and two theorems are unchanged, as are their proofs and Lemma A.1 in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable bias mitigation, fairness–capability trade-offs, applicability to VLMs and LLMs, and sparse interventions.

C2.justification: The substantive explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including the binary gender–occupation scope, capability trade-offs, increased abstention and exclusion of fine-tuning comparisons.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information in Appendices B–D is unchanged, including prompt templates, optimizer settings and the practical decision not to enforce a KL penalty during training. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 66 reference entries are unchanged. Bibliography pagination changes without altering citations or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds Barry-John Theobald to the author list, shortens two displayed author names, updates dates and adds Section 7, Acknowledgements. The research prose and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: One Table 2 cell changes from red to yellow, the author line reflows, and the acknowledgements shift the reference list's start from page 10 to page 11. Figures, table structures and appendix layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, theory, experimental evidence and reproducibility material remain unchanged. Attribution and layout edits have limited impact. Table 2 removes a misleading 'worsened' color, but its replacement 'within SEM' label is also unsupported by the displayed 10.3% (0.2) versus baseline 10.9% (0.2), leaving no meaningful overall quality improvement.
